minutes.headline: Personnel Committee agreed to draft a May town meeting article switching vacation accrual to front-loaded days; Wendy leads.
minutes.summary: The committee heard extended public comment from sewer commissioners and the sewer business manager about the job-rating process, and the chair stressed it is far from finished. It then discussed vacation leave accrual, agreeing informally to pursue a warrant article for the May town meeting. It also discussed outlier positions and planned next steps: reviewing the library and Council on Aging groups at the next meeting.

public_comment.topic: Questioned whether one rating system fits all jobs, asked for supervisor input and a joint meeting with the Sewer Commission before approval; concerned the sewer business manager is not on the outlier list.

Said there is still confusion about the process, that she and her supervisor rated her job differently and the job description is inaccurate; raised that hazard-related points are 23% of the score and that other towns' systems differ.

public_comment.stated_role: coordinator at the Council on Aging
public_comment.topic: Summarized how police, DPW, fire, municipal employee contracts and the 2010 SAP agreement handle vacation accrual in days versus hours, and said discrepancies exist.
Suggested that if vacation moves to days, sick time should also be changed to days for consistency.

votes.motion: Explore the vacation accrual change further, with Wendy taking the lead on drafting a May town meeting warrant article.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; Sue, Donna, Wendy and others said aye; no nays heard)

budget_items.what_was_said: Members said switching to front-loaded days would have no budget impact for these positions because pay is the same and there is no separate vacation budget.
A buy-back or payout option was noted as something that would affect the budget; use-it-or-lose-it was the stated preference.
Members agreed to set aside pay and salary grids until job rating and grades are settled, and noted no one's pay would be reduced.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee agreed by roll call, with no nays heard, to explore a change to vacation accrual, with Wendy leading a May town meeting warrant article.
Members said front-loading vacation days would have no budget impact for these positions, since pay is the same and there is no separate vacation budget.
The committee decided against joint meetings with individual commissions; disputes over job descriptions go through the HR Director and chain of command.
Sewer commissioners and the sewer business manager objected to the job-rating process in public comment; the chair said the process is far from finished.
Members agreed to set pay and salary grids aside until job ratings and grades are settled, and noted no one's pay would be reduced.

why_it_matters: If a vacation accrual article reaches the May town meeting warrant, residents will be asked to vote on it, and it would change how town employees earn leave.
The job-rating work will set the grades and salary grid for town positions, so its outcome shapes what the town pays staff in later budgets.
